caption_hook: 📸 Giant armadillos breed only once every 3 years. A camera trap in the Peruvian Amazon just filmed a baby. Follow for 3 good-news wins a day
question: One-word answer: which story would you tell your friends about first?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves weird animals

first_comment: Giant armadillos have the biggest claws of any living mammal, about 20 cm long. Had you ever heard of them before today?

stories.headline: A rare baby giant armadillo was filmed in the Amazon
stories.summary: A camera trap set with help from the Indigenous community of San Francisco caught a baby giant armadillo. Filming one can take over a year and hundreds of cameras.
stories.why: The footage will back a proposed law to protect the species in Loreto.

stories.headline: Scientists found up to 2.8 million eels on one seamount
stories.summary: Over 9 sonar surveys, CSIRO found a huge gathering of basketwork eels at Patience Seamount in Huon Marine Park, the only one of about 120 nearby seamounts with it.
stories.why: The females were ready to spawn, so this protected spot may be a key breeding site.

stories.headline: A painted-on liquid stopped tooth decay without a drill
stories.summary: In a trial of 830 children under 6, silver diamine fluoride painted on every 6 months stopped decay in more than half of their decayed baby teeth. No shots or drilling.
stories.why: The results give the maker the trial data it needs to seek FDA approval as a cavity drug.

stories.stat_label: of microplastics removed in lab tests
stories.headline: A plant-inspired filter will catch microplastics in sewage
stories.summary: PolyGone Systems, started by 2 Princeton graduates, copies how water-shedding plants trap particles. A 2-year pilot will run at the Atlantic County Utilities Authority.
stories.why: Wastewater is a major route for microplastics into the ocean.

fun_fact: A giant armadillo can weigh about 30 kg.
